caption:
What can you tell about a clinic before anyone speaks to you?
More than you would think, and most of it is near the floor.

Indoor slippers at the door mean they expect you to stay a while, not drop in. A blanket folded on the chair means someone already knew that treatment rooms run cold. Whether the consultation happens at a desk in the open or behind a door tells you what they think a consultation is for. And a bag handed over on the way out means aftercare was planned as part of the visit, rather than ending at reception.

None of it is decoration. All of it is an assumption the clinic has made about what is going to happen to you.

What this is not: a way to rank anywhere. Plenty of careful clinics are completely plain, and a beautiful room proves nothing. This is an observation of general clinic practice, not a research finding, and it does not describe any one clinic or country.

What it gives you is something to read while you wait, instead of the wall.

General education only.

#PatientExperience #ClinicVisit #PatientTips #MedicalAesthetics #KoreanAesthetics
first_comment: The slippers are the one nobody mentions and the one that tells you the most - they only exist if the clinic expects you to stay. What is the strangest thing you have seen in a waiting room?

Slide 2 of 8: Three empty waiting chairs against a plain wall. Nothing in the room is decoration.
Slide 3 of 8: Slippers at the door mean the clinic expects you to stay a while.
Slide 4 of 8: A blanket folded on a waiting chair, because treatment rooms run cold.
Slide 5 of 8: An open consult room door off a bright corridor. Notice whether the consult has a door.
Slide 6 of 8: A bag handed over on the way out means aftercare was planned.
Slide 7 of 8: A plain room is not a worse room. Observation, not a study finding.
